_about: Self-correction guidance for ruff findings, keyed by rule code. A code missing here falls back to its family (the leading letters: F, E, B, SIM, RUF, PERF). tools/ruff_sensor.py ships only the entries for rules that fired. Run `.venv/bin/ruff rule <CODE>` for ruff's own explanation.
F401: Unused import. Delete it. If the module re-exports the name on purpose, list it in `__all__` instead of suppressing.
F811: A name is defined twice and the first definition is dead. Delete the stale one; if both are needed, give them different names.
F821: Undefined name: this line raises NameError when it runs. Usually a typo, a missing import, or a variable used outside the branch that assigns it.
F841: A local variable is assigned and never read. Delete the assignment, or use the value. When unpacking, name the unused part `_`.
F: Pyflakes found code that is dead or broken at runtime (unused or undefined names, redefinitions, bad format strings). Fix the code, do not suppress: these are almost never false positives.
E401: Several modules imported on one line. Put each import on its own line.
E402: Import not at the top of the module. Move it up with the other imports. If it truly must run after setup code, suppress it with that reason: `# noqa: E402 -- <what must run first>`.
E711: Comparison to None with `==`/`!=`. Use `is None` / `is not None`; `==` can be overridden and lies.
E712: Comparison to True/False with `==`. Test the value directly (`if flag:`), or use `is True` only when the type really can be something other than bool.
E721: Type comparison with `==`. Use `isinstance(x, T)`, which also accepts subclasses.
E722: Bare `except:` also swallows KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit. Catch the specific exceptions this code can recover from. In a per-listing scraper loop, `except Exception` plus a logged warning is the house pattern.
E731: A lambda assigned to a name. Write a `def`: it gets a real name in tracebacks and can carry a docstring.
E741: Ambiguous name (`l`, `O`, `I`) that reads like 1 or 0. Rename it to say what it holds.
E: pycodestyle error (statement layout, imports, comparisons). Apply the fix ruff suggests; these are mechanical.
B006: Mutable default argument: the same list/dict is shared by every call and accumulates state. Default to None and create the object inside the function.
B007: Loop variable is never used in the body. Rename it to `_` (or `_name`) so the reader knows it is ignored on purpose.
B008: Function call in a default argument runs once, at import time, not per call. Typer's `typer.Option`/`typer.Argument` are already exempt in pyproject.toml; for anything else, default to None and call inside.
B009: `getattr(obj, "name")` with a constant name is just `obj.name`. Write the attribute access.
B011: `assert False` disappears under `python -O`. Raise an exception (`raise AssertionError(...)` or a specific error).
B017: `pytest.raises(Exception)` passes on any error, including the bug you are testing for. Raise and expect the specific exception type.
B018: A statement whose value is computed and thrown away. Usually a forgotten `return`, `assert`, or call parentheses.
B023: A closure inside a loop captures the loop variable by reference, so every closure sees its last value. Bind it as a default argument (`lambda x, item=item: ...`) or build the function outside the loop.
B904: `raise` inside `except` without `from`. Use `raise NewError(...) from err` to keep the original cause in the traceback, or `from None` when the original error is noise for the user (e.g. a clean CLI message).
B905: `zip()` without `strict=`. If both sequences must have the same length, pass `strict=True` so a mismatch fails loudly instead of silently truncating; pass `strict=False` only when truncation is intended.
B: flake8-bugbear found a likely bug or a design trap (shared mutable state, swallowed exceptions, late-binding closures). Read `.venv/bin/ruff rule <CODE>` and fix the cause; suppress only with a concrete reason.
SIM102: Nested `if` with no other statements: merge the conditions with `and`. One fewer nesting level.
SIM103: `if cond: return True / return False`. Return the condition (wrapped in `bool(...)` if it is not already a bool).
SIM105: `try/except: pass` to ignore one error. Use `contextlib.suppress(SpecificError)`, which states the intent in one line.
SIM108: `if/else` that only assigns one variable. Use a conditional expression, unless it would exceed one readable line.
SIM110: A loop that returns True on the first match. Use `any(...)` (or `all(...)` for the inverse).
SIM118: `key in d.keys()` builds a view for nothing. Write `key in d`.
SIM: flake8-simplify: the same logic can be written with fewer branches or names. Apply the simplification; it lowers complexity for the reader and for the `shape` sensor.
RUF005: List concatenation with `+` to build a new list. Use unpacking: `[*items, extra]`.
RUF010: `str()`/`repr()` inside an f-string. Use the conversion flag: `f"{x!r}"`.
RUF012: Mutable class attribute default is shared by all instances. Annotate it as `ClassVar[...]` if that is intended, otherwise set it in `__init__` or use a dataclass `field(default_factory=...)`.
RUF013: Parameter defaults to None but its annotation is not Optional. Annotate it `X | None` (or `Optional[X]`) so pyright checks the None case.
RUF015: `list(x)[0]` builds a whole list to read one item. Use `next(iter(x))`.
RUF022: `__all__` is not sorted. Run `ruff check --fix`; a sorted `__all__` makes merges and reviews trivial.
RUF100: A `# noqa` that no longer suppresses anything. Delete it (or the stale code in it). Stale suppressions hide the next real finding on that line.
RUF: Ruff-specific rule (stale suppressions, Optional annotations, unsorted __all__, mutable class attributes). Apply the fix; `ruff check --fix` handles many of them.
PERF401: A loop that only appends to a list. Use a list comprehension (or `list.extend` with a generator): faster and one expression to read.
PERF102: Iterating `d.items()` but using only keys or only values. Iterate `d` or `d.values()`.
PERF: Perflint: a loop pattern with a faster idiomatic form. Apply it unless the loop body is doing more than the rule assumes.
suppression: When a finding is genuinely wrong at this spot, suppress it on that line with a reason: `# noqa: CODE -- <why the rule does not apply here>`. The `shape` sensor fails any suppression without ` -- reason`, and RUF100 flags it once it stops suppressing anything.
